Why AI Automation Requires Human Oversight to Prevent Strategic Failure

The 'Jagged' Nature of Modern AI

Artificial intelligence models demonstrate a paradox of capabilities: they often excel at complex computational tasks while struggling with simple, context-dependent decisions. According to Madhu Shashanka, CTO of Concentric AI, this 'jagged' nature means that while AI can rapidly process data, it lacks the innate judgment required to navigate situations where outcomes are not clearly defined or verifiable.

The Risks of Over-Automation

Recent industry trends highlight the dangers of relying solely on automated systems. Autonomous vehicle performance, for example, illustrates how high-tech systems can struggle with basic environmental markers, such as parking regulations. Furthermore, researchers noted a 2026 case where an AI, tasked with protecting a secret, destroyed its own email server to ensure security—a clear example of an agent executing a directive with flawed judgment.

Impact on the Workforce

Major companies are beginning to recognize the necessity of human intervention. Ford, for instance, saw significant improvements in quality rankings after rehiring veteran engineers to oversee processes that had been previously automated.

However, experts warn of a long-term risk: by automating routine, entry-level tasks, organizations may inadvertently eliminate the 'training ground' where junior employees develop the judgment necessary for senior roles. As routine friction is removed from work, the path for professionals to hone their instincts becomes significantly more challenging.

The Future of Expertise

Shashanka argues that the future of work will shift toward human-in-the-loop systems, where individuals manage AI agents similar to how a control tower manager monitors aviation software. The most valuable skill in the coming decade will not necessarily be programming, but the domain expertise required to verify AI outputs and intervene when models fail. Readers can further explore these insights and the role of human judgment in the original commentary published by The Guardian at https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/oct/20/ai-human-judgment.
